1

Scope
for vanilla belonging to the-species Vani//a .fragrans (Salisbury) Ames,

This pan of ISO 5565 specifies requirements syn. Vanilla planifolia Andrews.

This part of ISO 5565 is applicable to vanilla in pods, bulk, cut or in the form of powder. It is not applicable to vanilla extracts. NOTE This vanilla is commonly known under the names associated with its geographic origin, namely Bourbon (from Madagascar, Comores and Reunion), Indonesian, Mexican, Tongan, Indian, Chinese and Ugandan vanilla.

5.1

General characteristics
Vanilla pods

Vanilla pods shall:
-- -- -- have the characteristics have undergone be dark chocolate corresponding to their qualitative category (see clause 6); their flavou~

a suitable treatment with a view to developing brown to reddish in colour.

The vanilla pods may be naturally frosted, due to the development on their surface of crystals of natural vanillin exclusively, and may have a mark at the bottom one-third of their length. They shall not: -- have undergone any treatment which could induce a change in their natural vanillin content or in the content of any other constituent of the flavou~ be moth-eaten, mouldy, creosoted, "poiquees" (blistered) or oxidized;

--

have an odour which is not typical of vanilla. 5.2 Cut vanilla

Pods or pieces are generally wooded, and may have several large stains. 5.4 Vanilla powder

Vanilla powder shall: -- -- -- be obtained from vanilla pods meeting the requirements specified in 5.1;

be sufficiently fine to pass through a sieve of aperture size 1,25 mm; be dark chocolate brown to reddish in colour;

IS 15460 (Part 1 ) :2004 ISO 5565-1 : 1999

--

have the natural and very marked flavour of vanilla.

It shall not:

--

have undergone any treatment which could induce a change in its natural vanillin content or in the content of any other constituents of the flavour; contain any extraneous matter;

--

have a musty or creosote odour, or any other odour which is not typical of vanilla.

7.2

Vanillin

content

The vanillin content mainly depends on the conditions under which the pods are cultivated, harvested and processed, and also on their length. The vanillin content usually observed, on a wet basis, is between 1,6 Y. and 2,4 % when determined by one of the methods described in 4.2 or 4.3 of ISO 5562-2:1999. Pods whose vanillin content is less than 1,6 % can be considered to have resulted from faulty processing. On the NOTE other hand, those whose vanillin content is greater than 2,4 O/. should be subjected to more intensive testing because of the possibility of adulteration by the addition of synthetic vanillin.

10 Packing and marking
10.1 Packing

10.1.1 Vanilla pods Vanilla pods shall be put in packets of pods of the same length, and shall then be put in clean, sound, watertight containers made of a material which will have no effect on the product (e.g. tin-plate boxes, waxed paper). Each of these elementary (according to clause 6). containers of packets of pods shall be uniform from the point of view of category

A series of these elementary containers, the contents of which are homogeneous, constitutes is constituted by either a homogeneous lot or by several lots belonging to different categories. 10.1.2 Cut vanilla

a lot. A consignment

Cut vanilla shall be put in packets of pods of the same length when they are sufficiently cannot be put in bundles. They shall then be placed in clean, sound and watertight containers the product. Cut vanilla shall be uniform from the botanical point of view. 10.1.3 Vanilla in bulk Vanilla in bulk shall be put in clean, sound and watertight containers the product. 10.1.4 Vanilla powder Vanilla powder shall be put in clean, sound and watertight on Ihe product. containers
